newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices hold ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices hold ahead of weekend.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly steady Friday in light trading, pressured by extended mild weather but boosted by another unexpected nuclear outage, sources said.
"It's a liquidity trap. A lot of people are going into the month pretty balanced. There aren't a lot of daily players out there," one market source said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to dip to below-normal levels late Saturday and into Sunday but then moderate to slightly-above normal levels next week.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Monday were steady in the $15.50-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, with offers heard as high as $19.
Firm, off-peak power into TVA was still talked at $13.50-14.00.
Lending support to the market was the unscheduled outage at Virginia Power's 781 megawatt (MW) Surry 1 nuclear power unit. The company said the unit would likely restart in a few days.
TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., restarted after tripping off line Wednesday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Monday delivery were flat to higher in the $21.50-22.50 per MWh range.
Weekend deliveries in Florida on a 16-hour schedule hovered in the $21.00-22.00 area for firm, peak power.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $14.00 per MWh.
Florida Power and Light's 839 MW St Lucie 2 nuclear power unit, which had been running at 90 percent, has resumed full output.
Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, is expected to resume power output this weekend.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
All three units are in Seneca, S.C.
Despite firm power prices, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast pipes fell by more than 30 cents to about $2.60 per million British thermal units.
